results.evidence:
InviteRow adds `inviteEmailErrors[index] ? ' errored'` to the input class and renders `
{inviteEmailErrors[index]}
`. The selector flags emails found in `members`.
The selector computes `ownEmail = user?.email?.toLowerCase()` and returns "You can't invite yourself" when `email === ownEmail`. It also flags before members load.

`canSubmit` becomes false, but no submit control is shown communicating a reason such as 'remove existing members'. The per-row Submit button is still only `disabled={!isEmail(invitesToSend[index].target_email)}`, so it stays enabled for a member row. The batch submit button and the onboarding step are not changed in the patch.
`const email = target_email.trim().toLowerCase()` is compared against a Set of lowercased member emails.

`afterMount(({ actions }) => { actions.ensureAllMembersLoaded() })` runs when the logic mounts, and the own-email check uses `user`, which does not depend on the members data. I could not confirm that `ensureAllMembersLoaded` exists in membersLogic, but the connect refers to it.

The check moved into `validate_target_email`, which runs at validation. The bulk view is not shown, so I can't confirm it validates every row before any `create()` call. That is the behaviour the criterion needs.

`raise exceptions.ValidationError("A user with this email address already belongs to the organization.", code="existing_email_address")` inside `validate_target_email` produces a field error on target_email with a stable code.
Nothing changes how failures are reported to error tracking. The frontend loader failure path is unchanged, and there is no filtering of the existing-member code.
There is no failure listener in inviteLogic that reloads members when the server rejects with existing_email_address. Members are only loaded in afterMount.

result:
Inviting an existing member (or yourself) is now flagged on the row as you type and rejected up front on submit. I didn't run the tests, the type check or the linters, so none of this has been run.

**Backend** (`posthog/api/organization_invite.py`)
- The "already a member" check used to run inside `create()`, after earlier rows in the batch were already saved and emailed.
- It now runs in `validate_target_email`, so a bulk request fails at `is_valid()` before anything is created or sent.
- A single-invite request that hits an existing member is rejected the same way.
- The error is a normal 400 validation error with code `existing_email_address`, not an unexpected exception, so it no longer goes to error tracking as one.
- I added `test_bulk_invite_with_existing_member_creates_no_invites` in `posthog/api/test/test_organization_invites.py`. It sends two valid emails plus your own email in upper case, and checks for a 400, no new invites and no emails sent.

**Frontend** (`inviteLogic.ts` and `InviteModal.tsx`, which both the onboarding step and the settings dialog use)
- `inviteLogic` now loads the organization's members and your own user.
- A new `inviteEmailErrors` selector returns a message per row. It shows "You can't invite yourself" for your own email and "This person is already a member of the organization" for a current member. Matching ignores case.
- The affected row gets the error styling and shows the message under the input.
- `canSubmit` is false while any row has one of these errors, so the batch can't be sent until you fix or remove it.
- The members list is loaded once when the logic mounts. If a very large organization's member list isn't fully loaded on the client, the server check still catches it.

I hand-edited the kea-typegen interface block at the top of `inviteLogic.ts` to match, rather than regenerating it.
